title: 栅栏行拖动通知建议
instruction:
您是 Ragnhild Laurent，Viktor Kirchner 的律师，Viktor Kirchner 是 Palisade Row Storage 的 12% 少数派成员。管理成员弗洛里安·奥耶拉兰 (Florian Oyelaran) 向维克多发出了一份与涉及所有六个存储设施的拟议出售有关的拖带通知。维克托在收到通知后有十四天的时间签署交易文件或维护异议者的权利，他需要一个可以采取行动的答案，而不是一系列可能性。我在为公司提供建议时起草了2017运营协议，因此建议必须披露之前的角色，并坦诚地对待我所写语言的专业判断。控制来源为附件`palisade_row_storage_2017_operating_agreement.pdf`；将其视为唯一提供的公司记录，不得发明其不包含的交易条款、估值数字、程序事实或法律权威。为 Viktor 准备一封客户建议信，另存为`viktor_kirchner_drag_along_advice.docx`，并保存配套的 PDF 为`viktor_kirchner_drag_along_advice.pdf`；将这两个文件写入解算器启动的工作目录的顶层，并使用这些文件名。
这封信是写给 Viktor 的，只有在适当的情况下才可以与 Rookwood Partners 和 Hollowpine Holdings 分享，因此请使用简单但在法律上准确的语言，并将协议规定的内容与尚不确定的内容区分开来。完成的信件不要超过四页，包括任何简短的表格或标注，并使其可供未重新阅读协议的客户使用。对建议或决策点进行编号，以便维克托能够快速找到他必须采取的行动。你的信必须给出一个明确的建议——签署拖拽或反对意见——而不是提供一个未排名的菜单。解释该建议是如何根据拖累条款、协议的定义和交易条款、通知和时间条款以及公司出售与解散后的资产出售相比的可用处理方式得出的。提出反对你的建议的最强烈的解读以及支持它的解读，并解释如果法院采用其他解读对维克托的实际后果。仅当协议或提供的通知相关语言支持时，才将十四天的截止日期陈述为事实，确定可能改变建议的任何假设或遗漏事实，并且不要用捏造的事实来填补这些空白。
此事正处于实践中的变化中：该信函必须在十四天的决策窗口内有用，并且仍然明确在交易结束或公司解散后建议的立场意味着什么。有关执行机制、税务、估值和交易管理的一些问题属于其他顾问或职能部门；标记界限，不要假装在记录或你的角色之外提供建议。包括简明的风险和选项解释、维克托在截止日期前应采取的行动、他应保留或要求的文件或确认书，以及协议支持的任何权利保留。不要引用虚构的案例，不要声明异议者的权利保证特定的支付，如果对资产出售和解散的处理不明确，不要声称该条款是明确的，并且不要以模糊的后续步骤清单而不是决定结束。确保 DOCX 和 PDF 表述相同的内容、使用相同的数字和日期，并且呈现时清晰易读。

---

上面提到的文件在`references/`中：

- `references/palisade_row_storage_2017_operating_agreement.pdf` — 用于解释拖带条款、所有权、定义、交易机制、通知时间、解散、分配、争议条款和相关会员权利的唯一公司记录。
将您完成的工作写入**当前工作目录的顶层**，使用以下文件名：

- `viktor_kirchner_drag_along_advice.docx` — 一封完整的客户建议信，为 Viktor 提供关于签署拖欠协议或维护异议者权利的可行建议。 （起始工作目录的顶层；包括表格或标注在内不超过四页；法律上精确、客户可读且与 PDF 内部一致。）
- `viktor_kirchner_drag_along_advice.pdf` — 渲染、匹配的客户建议信 PDF 版本。 （起始工作目录的顶层；内容必须与 DOCX 匹配，包括日期、百分比、金额、定义术语、建议和警告；清晰且不超过四页。）

除了这些文件名之外，不会收集任何内容。在其他地方或以任何其他名称编写的正确文件得分为零。

materials.text:
OPERATING AGREEMENT
                             PALISADE ROW STORAGE, LLC
                                                Effective 1 July 2017

1. Members and Definitions
1.1 The Company. Palisade Row Storage, LLC (the “Company”) owns and operates six self-storage facilities as
one storage business. This Agreement is the complete agreement of its Members on the subjects it addresses.
1.2 Members and Percentage Interests. Florian Oyelaran, Managing Member: 58%; Viktor Kirchner: 12%;
Rookwood Partners: 18%; Hollowpine Holdings: 12%. Percentage Interests govern voting, allocations, and
distributions unless this Agreement expressly says otherwise.
1.3 “Company” means Palisade Row Storage, LLC, including its business, property, rights, and obligations, but not
a Member individually.
1.4 “Sale of the Company” means a direct or indirect transfer of more than 50% of the outstanding Percentage
Interests, or a merger or other entity-level transaction in which the holders of a majority of Percentage Interests
immediately before the transaction cease to hold a majority of interests in the surviving entity. A disposition by
the Company of one or more assets is not expressly included or excluded by this definition.
1.5 “Major Transaction” means (a) a Sale of the Company, (b) a merger, or (c) a sale, lease, exchange, or other
disposition of all or substantially all of the Company’s business assets, in one transaction or a related series.
1.6 “Dissent Notice” means a written notice under Section 5.5 stating that the Member dissents from a proposed
Major Transaction, identifying the notice received, and reserving the Member’s rights under this Agreement.

2. Management and Approval
2.1 Florian Oyelaran is the Managing Member. He may conduct ordinary-course business and must give notice
and obtain the stated approvals for a Major Transaction.
2.2 A Major Transaction requires written approval of the Managing Member and Members holding at least 75% of
Percentage Interests. Approval authorizes the Company to pursue and implement the approved Major
Transaction, subject to Sections 5.4 and 5.5. This Section does not say that every approved Major Transaction is a
Sale of the Company.

3. Transfers and Implementation
3.1 No voluntary transfer of a Membership Interest is effective unless permitted by this Agreement or approved
under Section 2.2. A Member shall execute instruments reasonably necessary to carry out a transaction that this
Agreement makes binding on that Member.
3.2 This Section alone does not require a Member to approve a Major Transaction or surrender a Membership
Interest. Section 5.4 supplies the special rule for a Sale of the Company.

4. Notices
4.1 Notices must be in writing and delivered personally, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by
electronic mail to the last designated address or email. Receipt occurs upon personal delivery, recorded courier
delivery, or an email not returned as undeliverable.
4.2 A Major Transaction notice must describe the proposed form, identify whether it is asserted to be a Sale of the
Company, and provide material transaction documents then available. A notice under Section 5.4 or 5.5 must
state the fourteenth (14th) day after receipt as the response date.

5. Major Transactions; Drag-Along; Dissent
5.1 Following Section 2.2 approval, the Managing Member may deliver a transaction notice. The notice starts the
Article 5 response process; it does not characterize a disposition contrary to the transaction documents.
5.2 In a Sale of the Company, each Member shall receive the same form of consideration per Percentage Interest,
except for differences required by law or approved in writing by the affected Member.
5.3 An approved Major Transaction involving Company assets may be implemented by the Company. Proceeds
remain Company property until applied or distributed under Article 6. An asset disposition does not become a
Membership Interest transfer merely because it concerns all or substantially all business assets.
5.4 Drag-Along in a Sale of the Company. If a Sale of the Company has been approved under Section 2.2, each
Member shall, on written notice, vote for, consent to, and execute agreements and instruments reasonably
necessary to complete that Sale of the Company, including an assignment of that Member’s Membership Interest.
Each Member shall respond by the fourteenth (14th) day after receipt. A Member who does not timely execute
required documents may be treated, solely to complete that Sale of the Company, as appointing the Managing

                             Palisade Row Storage — confidential agreement-based material
 Member attorney-in-fact to execute them; this remedy does not waive a timely Dissent Notice under Section 5.5 if
that Section applies.
5.5 A Member receiving notice of a proposed Major Transaction that is not a Sale of the Company subject to
Section 5.4 may deliver a Dissent Notice by the fourteenth (14th) day after receipt. A timely Dissent Notice does
not prevent the Company from completing an approved Major Transaction, but preserves the Member’s right to
contest whether Section 5.4 applies and to receive any Article 6 distribution. No appraisal formula, purchase
price, or guaranteed payment is created for a dissenting Member. Failure to give timely Dissent Notice consents
to the proposed Major Transaction but does not supply terms absent from transaction documents.

6. Dissolution, Winding Up, and Distributions
6.1 The Company dissolves upon written approval required by Section 2.2 to dissolve, upon a sale or disposition
of all or substantially all Company assets followed by a decision to wind up, or as otherwise required by law. An
asset sale does not automatically dissolve the Company before the applicable decision to wind up.
6.2 After dissolution, the Managing Member shall wind up affairs, collect and apply Company assets, discharge or
provide for Company liabilities, and make distributions under Section 6.3.
6.3 Cash or other property available after payment or provision for Company liabilities and winding-up expenses
shall be distributed to Members in proportion to their Percentage Interests. This Section does not establish an
amount or timing of distribution.

7. Construction, Amendment, and Disputes
7.1 This Agreement is read as a whole. A specific provision controls over a general one when both address the
same subject.
7.2 Amendment requires a writing approved by the Managing Member and Members holding at least 75% of
Percentage Interests; no amendment may disproportionately reduce a Member’s distribution percentage without
that Member’s written consent.
7.3 Members shall confer in good faith about disputes. A timely written reservation of rights does not waive a
Member’s ability to seek a determination under this Agreement.




                             Palisade Row Storage — confidential agreement-based material

gold.text:
CONFIDENTIAL — CLIENT ADVICE
Ragnhild Laurent
Counsel
To: Viktor Kirchner
Re: Palisade Row Storage — drag-along notice for proposed transaction involving all six facilities
Source: Palisade Row Storage, LLC Operating Agreement (2017) (the “Agreement”)
Recommendation at a glance
DECISION
DISSENT — deliver a timely Dissent Notice, rather than sign drag documents, on the present record.
Florian Oyelaran, the Managing Member, has served you with a drag-along notice concerning a proposed transaction involving all six Company facilities. You hold 12% of Palisade Row Storage. The Agreement requires a response by the fourteenth (14th) day after receipt of the applicable notice. This advice uses only the 2017 Agreement; I have not been given the notice, transaction documents, proof of service, approval records, or facts establishing the deal’s legal form.
1. Why I recommend dissent now
Section 5.4 makes the execution duty conditional: “If a Sale of the Company has been approved under Section 2.2,” each Member must consent, vote, and execute documents reasonably necessary to complete that Sale, including an interest assignment. A qualifying approval requires Florian and at least 75% of Percentage Interests (Section 2.2). The notice should identify whether the deal is asserted to be a Sale of the Company and provide material documents then available (Section 4.2). We lack those facts, so I do not assume either compliance or approval.
Transaction form is decisive. “Company” is Palisade Row Storage, LLC, not the facilities (Section 1.3). “Sale of the Company” means a majority interest transfer or listed entity-level transaction (Section 1.4). A Major Transaction separately includes an all-or-substantially-all asset sale (Section 1.5), and Section 5.3 says an asset sale is carried out by the Company and does not become an interest transfer merely because it covers the business assets. The Agreement is silent about whether an asset sale followed by dissolution is a “Sale of the Company” for Section 5.4. That unresolved line favors preserving your dissent position, not accepting an irreversible interest-transfer obligation.
2. Competing constructions
The enforcing reading has force: the six facilities comprise one business; a coordinated sale of all, followed by winding up, has the practical end of a company sale. Section 2.2 authorizes an approved Major Transaction at the 75% threshold, and Article 5 aims to make an approved exit workable. A court could infer that a member should not defeat an approved exit simply because it uses assets rather than interests.
The limiting reading is stronger on the text. Section 5.4 repeatedly says “Sale of the Company”; Section 1.4 specifies entity-interest and entity-level events; Sections 1.5 and 5.3 separately identify asset dispositions. Section 3.2 confirms that implementation language alone does not surrender an interest. Those distinctions matter: an asset sale leaves proceeds with the Company until Article 6, while a company sale transfers membership interests. Treating every all-asset sale as a drag would diminish the separate Dissent Notice mechanism in Section 5.5. The clause is not unambiguous as to an asset sale followed by dissolution.
3. Risks and the opposite result
If a court adopts the enforcing reading, Section 5.4 binds you to execute reasonably necessary drag documents after a qualifying approved Sale; a timely Dissent Notice does not stop an approved Major Transaction (Section 5.5), and the Managing Member may use the limited attorney-in-fact remedy to complete a qualifying sale. The practical risk of dissent is that the transaction closes without your signature while you face uncertainty and cost over whether the drag applied.
If a court adopts the limiting reading, the drag does not bind you in an asset sale followed by dissolution. The Company may still complete an approved asset Major Transaction, but your Dissent Notice preserves the Section 5.4 issue and Article 6 distribution rights. It supplies neither a veto nor an appraisal formula, purchase price, or guaranteed payment. The practical risk of signing is accepting an interest-transfer framework before the records establish one, weakening your ability to keep the Agreement’s asset/company distinction. As a 12% minority member, the targeted Section 5.5 procedure is more protective. Signing is not equally advisable because it relinquishes that procedural position while the form is unresolved.
4. Action before the response date
Before the fourteenth (14th) day after receipt, deliver a written Dissent Notice under Section 5.5 by a permitted Section 4.1 method. Identify the notice, state that the all-facility transaction appears to be an asset transaction unless documents establish otherwise, and reserve your right to contest Section 5.4’s application and receive any Article 6 distribution. Do not state approval of a membership-interest sale. Preserve the drag notice, delivery evidence, the 2017 Agreement, transaction-document versions, and communications.
Request written confirmation of (i) transaction form—interest transfer/entity-level transaction or asset sale; (ii) Section 2.2 written approval and percentage-interest calculation; (iii) whether the notice invokes Section 5.4 or 5.5; and (iv) whether dissolution and winding up follow closing. These are missing facts that could change the advice. A reservation is grounded in Sections 5.5 and 7.3; it does not contradict dissent or prevent an approved transaction.
5. Transition and post-closing position
This is a practice mid-change: the decision window precedes final form, closing, and any dissolution. Dissent is the immediate procedural choice, not a prediction that the Company cannot sell facilities. If it later dissolves, Section 6.1 requires the applicable decision to wind up; Section 6.2 directs the Managing Member to settle liabilities; and Section 6.3 distributes what is available after liabilities and winding-up expenses in Percentage Interests. Your 12% therefore governs allocation of what is available if Article 6 applies, not a dollar amount, date, valuation, or priority beyond those terms. If documents establish a qualifying Sale of the Company, reassessment is required before an inconsistent execution position.
6. Disclosure and scope
I drafted the 2017 Operating Agreement while advising the Company. That matters because I wrote language now requiring construction. I have identified both readings candidly and base this advice on the recorded text and structure, not unrecorded drafting intent. This is advice to you and may be shared with Rookwood Partners and Hollowpine Holdings only as appropriate; it is not advice to them or the Company. It interprets the supplied Agreement only. Transaction-document negotiation, execution mechanics, closing administration, tax, and valuation require the responsible advisers and information outside this record.
Decision
My clear recommendation is: DISSENT. Deliver the Section 5.5 Dissent Notice before the fourteenth (14th) day after receipt, preserve the records, and request the listed confirmations. This protects your 12% member position while the Agreement’s unresolved line between a Sale of the Company and an asset sale followed by dissolution is tested; it does not promise payment or prevent a properly approved transaction from proceeding.
Ragnhild Laurent
Counsel to Viktor Kirchner

spec.professional_context: This is a minority-member advice package prepared during a live transaction and a change in the company’s operating state. The reviewer needs a defensible construction of an ambiguous drag clause, a clear client decision, and careful limits around transaction, tax, valuation, and administration issues handled by other functions.
difficulty_sources: Interpreting an ambiguous drag-along condition against defined terms and dissolution provisions
Committing to one client recommendation while fairly presenting the strongest opposing construction
Transforming one operating agreement into a concise advice letter and matching PDF
Disclosing prior drafting involvement and marking boundaries with tax, valuation, and transaction administration functions

source_construction.purpose: Create one internally consistent synthetic operating agreement for Palisade Row Storage. It should include the company name, six-facility business description, Viktor Kirchner’s 12% membership interest, Florian Oyelaran’s managing-member role, the 2017 date, and the relevant defined terms.
required_substance: Include a drag-along clause conditioned on a sale of the Company, with a controlling-member approval mechanism and ordinary execution obligations.

Define Company and Sale of the Company in language that supports a plausible argument that a sale of substantially all business assets may or may not qualify, but do not resolve the asset-sale-followed-by-dissolution question expressly.
Include provisions on member approval, notice, the fourteen-day election or response period, dissenters’ rights or an equivalent contractual election, and the effect of failing to respond.
Include transaction implementation language that makes the drag’s consequences relevant to a member signing or refusing.
Include dissolution, winding-up, and distribution provisions sufficient to analyze Viktor’s position after an asset sale followed by dissolution.

Include conflict, amendment, and dispute or construction provisions only where they help a lawyer reason from the agreement; avoid adding a controlling clause that makes the central ambiguity disappear.
Use only synthetic identifiers and no real addresses, account numbers, or external authorities.
imperfections: The agreement must be complete and mutually consistent but deliberately silent or structurally ambiguous about whether an asset sale followed by dissolution is a sale of the Company for drag purposes.
The notice language and transaction provisions should create a genuine interpretive tension without containing a hidden answer.
The agreement should not supply a transaction price or other invented economic facts.

gold_derivation.method: Have a domain-expert lawyer draft a four-page-or-shorter client advice letter from the agreement, then independently review it against every rubric item and render both formats.
gold_derivation.intended_verdict: The gold must choose exactly one of sign or dissent, explain both plausible constructions, disclose the drafting role, describe the opposite-reading consequence for Viktor, and give a practical action inside fourteen days. The exact recommendation may be selected by the expert based on the constructed agreement’s balance, but the reasoning must be coherent and agreement-grounded.
gold_derivation.cross_file_rule: Generate the PDF from the reviewed DOCX or compare both after rendering; all names, percentages, dates, defined terms, caveats, and the recommendation must match.
quality_review: Verify that no rubric criterion depends on an unstated transaction amount, private code, or external live source.
Verify that the letter does not guarantee a dissenters’ payment, invent authorities, or overstep into tax, valuation, or administrative advice.
Verify the transition-period and post-dissolution consequences are both addressed.
Verify the final paragraph is a decision, not an unranked next-steps list.

reference_files.purpose: The sole company record for construing the drag-along provision, ownership, definitions, transaction mechanics, notice timing, dissolution, distributions, dispute provisions, and related member rights.
reference_files.discovery: Read this PDF before drafting; do not assume facts not stated in it.

original_instruction:
You are Ragnhild Laurent, counsel to Viktor Kirchner, a 12% minority member of Palisade Row Storage. Florian Oyelaran, the managing member, has served Viktor with a drag-along notice in connection with a proposed sale involving all six storage facilities. Viktor has fourteen days from receipt of the notice to sign the transaction documents or assert dissenters’ rights, and he needs an answer he can act on rather than a catalogue of possibilities. I drafted the 2017 operating agreement when I was advising the company, so the advice must disclose that prior role and deal candidly with the professional judgment involved in construing language I wrote. The governing source is the attached `palisade_row_storage_2017_operating_agreement.pdf`; treat it as the only supplied company record and do not invent transaction terms, valuation figures, procedural facts, or legal authorities that it does not contain. Prepare a client advice letter for Viktor, saved as `viktor_kirchner_drag_along_advice.docx`, and a matching PDF saved as `viktor_kirchner_drag_along_advice.pdf`; write both files into the top level of the working directory the solver starts in, using exactly those filenames. The letter is for Viktor and may be shared with Rookwood Partners and Hollowpine Holdings only as appropriate, so use plain but legally precise language and distinguish what the agreement establishes from what remains uncertain. Keep the completed letter to no more than four pages, including any short table or callout, and make it usable by a client who has not reread the agreement. Number the recommendations or decision points so Viktor can find the action he must take quickly. Your letter must give one clear recommendation—sign the drag or dissent—rather than presenting an unranked menu. Explain how the recommendation follows from the drag clause, the agreement’s definitions and transaction provisions, the notice and timing provisions, and the available treatment of a sale of the Company as compared with an asset sale followed by dissolution. Address the strongest reading against your recommendation as well as the reading supporting it, and explain the practical consequence for Viktor if a court adopts the other reading.
